title: Texas's 20th Congressional District General Election, 2026
jurisdiction: Texas's 20th Congressional District (San Antonio and Bexar County)
description: The general election for Texas's 20th Congressional District pits seven-term Democratic incumbent Joaquin Castro against Republican nominee Edgardo Baez. After redistricting, the seat now covers more of downtown San Antonio and remains the city's only reliably Democratic congressional district (Cook PVI: D+16). Castro, a senior member of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs Committees, has represented the district since 2013, while Baez, a U.S. Army veteran and first-time candidate, is challenging on a platform of economic development, public safety, and opposition to socialism. The March primary saw Castro defeat two little-known Democratic challengers with 88% of the vote, while Baez advanced from the Republican primary to set up the November contest.

candidates.name: Joaquin Castro
candidates.summary: Joaquin Castro is a seven-term U.S. Representative for Texas's 20th Congressional District, first elected in 2012. He serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and was previously recognized by the Center for Effective Lawmaking as the most effective Democratic House member in the 118th Congress. Before Congress, he served five terms in the Texas House of Representatives for District 125 and worked as a private attorney.

candidates.name: Edgardo Baez
candidates.summary: Edgardo Baez is a U.S. Army veteran, retired medical professional, criminal defense attorney, and published author making his first run for public office as the Republican nominee for Texas's 20th Congressional District. His career includes service as a combat medic, airborne paratrooper, and drill sergeant in the Army, followed by work as an ICU nurse and over 20 years as a criminal defense lawyer in San Antonio. Baez campaigns on a platform of economic development, public safety, education reform, border security, and opposition to socialism, and has pledged to support term limits on Congress.

forecast.rationale: TX-20 has a Cook PVI of D+16 and is described as San Antonio's only reliably Democratic congressional district. Incumbent Joaquin Castro is a seven-term Democrat who won his 2026 primary with 88% of the vote. Republican challenger Edgardo Baez is a first-time candidate. There are zero public numeric polls available for this race, which limits confidence. However, the district's strong Democratic partisan lean, combined with Castro's deep incumbency advantage and committee seniority (House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs), creates an overwhelming Democratic advantage. A safe Democratic hold is the most probable outcome, though the absence of polling tempers confidence slightly.
